Kharge cited alarming statistics related to pollution-linked deaths and unspent environmental funds in the city. He also mentioned the Supreme Court's directive to states to address pollution concerns within two weeks.
title: 'Why are we becoming Vishwaguru in air pollution?' Congress questions PM Modi

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Qantas is planning to outsource around 850 head-office jobs to Accenture, significantly affecting its Australian workforce. This transition will involve business functions like finance, human resources, and marketing being delivered from India. Employees have expressed concerns about job security, as assurances previously given by Qantas are being contradicted. The airline aims to retain employees through redeployment and retraining opportunities as part of this agreement.
title: Australian airline Qantas to axe 850 jobs at HQ, shift work to India

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: India is focusing on domestic maintenance, repair and overhaul capabilities to improve military readiness and reduce foreign reliance. The Indian Navy and Indian Air Force are working on several projects for indigenisation and serviceability. There are also initiatives to support foreign military operators through new facilities and agreements. Companies like Tata Advanced Systems and Lockheed Martin are involved in establishing support centers for various aircraft.
title: Keeping the edge sharp: India looks to build a global military MRO hub

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Security levels have been raised at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath in Britain following possible threats. Notable aircraft movements from Mildenhall, including the relocation of KC-135 Stratotankers and CV-22B Ospreys, have sparked concerns. Given previous incidents related to Iranian threats, authorities have cautioned residents to remain alert and report any suspicious actions surrounding the military installations to bolster safety measures.
title: Mystery threat puts US bases in Britain on high alert, aircraft shifted

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Researchers found that heavy rainfall can double the speed of Sít’ Kusá Glacier in Alaska, indicating significant changes in glacier behavior. During rainfall events, the glacier experiences surges lasting longer than previously observed, impacting its overall dynamics. Drainage efficiency is crucial as it influences how water interacts with the glacier, affecting its movement. Increased rainfall linked to climate change may lead to more frequent glacier accelerations in the future.
title: Heavy rainfall can speed up Alaskan glacier by 215%, study finds

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: A significant conservation achievement is on the horizon for the critically endangered Jamaican rock iguana as the National Environment and Planning Agency prepares to release 114 head-started iguanas back into their natural environment on November 14. This effort is the culmination of successful strategies aimed at boosting their dwindling population from fewer than 50 in 1990 through methods like captive rearing, habitat safeguards, and predator control.
title: Once thought extinct, rare Jamaican iguana nears 1,000th release into wild

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: A luxurious estate in Malibu, previously owned by Teodoro Nguema Obiang, was sold for an impressive $93.5 million following a corruption settlement. Initially bought for $30 million, the mansion changed hands several times amid legal challenges. Luxury developer Mauricio Oberfeld acquired and revamped it before it eventually became the property of the Stark family, known for their association with Chrome Hearts.
title: Malibu estate bought for $30m by African president's son sells for $93.5m

description: A retired Navy SEAL commander in New Hampshire paid a $1,000 fine after two felony charges over the removal of a boundary hemlock were dropped. title: Ex-Navy SEAL charged over lakefront tree removal; felonies dropped, $1,000 fine

description: Phil Wong, a councilman in New York City, has decided to withdraw his endorsement of the Delivery Protection Act, citing fears over potential job losses and the risk of businesses shutting down due to the bill. This legislation aims to require companies to employ delivery workers full-time instead of using subcontractors.

Mitchell Starc defends his earlier statements, refuting Khawaja's claims, while Alyssa Healy shares her mixed emotions over the renewed attention on the scandal. Cricket Australia appears disinclined to revisit past events, focusing instead on future endeavors.

With a remarkable net collection of Rs 346.35 crore in India over five days and a worldwide gross touching Rs 663.90 crore, the film is on a path to reaching Rs 700 crore post-Monday's earnings. Advance sales for Day 6 look strong as audience interest continues to grow.
title: 'Ramayana' box office day 6 (LIVE): Ranbir Kapoor starrer inches towards Rs 400 crore

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: The Indian Air Force achieved a significant milestone by landing an IL-76MD at Nyoma, which is 13,629 feet high. This accomplishment showcases the aircraft's capability to operate near the Line of Actual Control. Challenges remain regarding the operational availability and maintenance of the IL-76 fleet. Future assessments include extending the aircraft's operational life and possibly upgrading engines and avionics.
title: 40 years, a world record, but an uncertain future: What's next for IAF's IL-76?

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Adding to the public discourse, Michael Clarke has urged Cricket Australia to reconsider the Sandpapergate scandal investigation. Usman Khawaja's autobiography alleges that every member of the Australian Test team knew about the ball-tampering. David Warner supports this assertion, in contrast to Mitch Starc, who upholds the bowlers' past position. Nonetheless, CA dismisses the need for a new inquiry, reaffirming its satisfaction with the initial results, even after eight years.
title: ‘Fans have not moved on’: Clarke joins Sandpapergate storm as pressure mounts on CA

author: SANJAY SHARMA
description: ICSE Class 10 timetable 2027: CISCE has released the ICSE Class 10 timetable 2027, with examinations scheduled from February 15 to March 31. The subject-wise schedule includes English, Mathematics, Science, History and Civics, Geography, languages and elective papers. The board has revised examination timings, with reading time beginning at 10:00 AM and writing at 10:15 AM for regular morning papers. Candidates must carry their admission cards, follow examination guidelines and avoid prohibited electronic devices. Results are expected in April or May 2027.

title: Rishabh Pant to leave for New Zealand after Wednesday’s simulation

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: Sonia Gandhi reveals in her memoir that she has had minimal contact with PM Narendra Modi. Their encounters are restricted to formal greetings at political gatherings, often avoiding eye contact. Gandhi contrasts her vision of an inclusive India with Modi's more exclusionary ideology shaped by the RSS. She also revisits the violence of the 2002 Gujarat riots during Modi's tenure as chief minister.
title: 'No real contact': Sonia's memoir recalls face-to-face meetings with PM Modi

description: ISC Class 12 timetable 2027 released: CISCE has released the ISC Class 12 timetable for the 2027 board examinations, scheduled from February 9 to April 8. ISC Class 12 results are expected to be announced in April or May 2027.

description: As the chilly November nights arrive, sky enthusiasts will be treated to the dazzling display of three meteor showers, featuring the Northern Taurids and Leonids. Keep your eyes on the heavens on November 15 and 16 for the close alignment of Mars and Jupiter. The month culminates in the enchanting supermoon on November 24, heralding a series of three.
title: Mars and Jupiter to appear close together before sunrise on November 15 and 16

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Wade and Teresa King are challenging a substantial penalty of $267,540, which has been imposed due to alleged damage to wetlands. They argue that the locations in question are traditional stockwater ponds beneficial for their livestock. Meanwhile, the Washington State Department of Ecology asserts that the Kings harmed rare alkali wetlands through excavation. The couple fears restoration costs could exceed $3.7 million, jeopardizing their family ranch's future.
title: Washington couple fights $267,540 wetlands fine, faces $3.7m restoration bill

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: In a call for improved communication, UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting stressed the importance of engaging directly with Russia's military to avoid dire miscalculations. The backdrop of rising tensions due to accusations of state-sponsored terrorism has stirred security apprehensions across Britain. While London seeks to restore diplomatic channels, Moscow is resistant, favoring reduced UK engagement. Meanwhile, France and Germany pursue renewed ties with Russian authorities.
title: UK seeks military hotline with Russia amid fears accidental clash could spark war

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: HS Phoolka voices his concerns over Sonia Gandhi's memoir addressing the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and Operation Blue Star. He contests her claims about the Army's intervention timing post-Indira Gandhi's assassination, citing historical documentation. Furthermore, he questions her emotional depiction of Indira Gandhi after the operation, supported by Justice VM Tarkunde's report. Phoolka underscored that key military figures failed to arrive promptly, which could have averted the loss of life.
title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: BJP's Phoolka questions Army timeline, Indira's tears on 1984 riots

description: Construction of border barriers in Texas's Big Bend region will continue following a Supreme Court ruling. The ruling allows the Trump administration to resume work while a legal challenge is ongoing. Environmental groups and local stakeholders have expressed concerns regarding the project's impact on the region's landscape and ecology. Challenges to the federal government's authority to issue waivers under environmental laws remain unresolved.
title: Supreme Court allows Trump's Texas border wall work to resume after 38 days

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: In a recent election, California voters decisively shot down Proposition 40, which sought to enforce a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of billionaires. The Democratic leadership expressed concerns over the potential negative impacts on the economy and state finances. The opposition raised an astounding $333 million, heavily funded by prominent billionaires. Younger voters were in favor, while older generations stood firmly against it, showcasing a generational divide.

Esha Singh led the Indian team with a top score of 590, while Manu Bhaker and Divya Subbaraju contributed important scores. Both Esha and Manu qualified for the individual final, creating further opportunities for additional medals and Olympic quota places.

description: Former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi has recalled how Pranab Mukherjee hinted at his ambition to become prime minister during a 2010 conversation, leaving her "shocked". Her account in her memoir has drawn a sharp response from Mukherjee's daughter Sharmishtha, who questioned Sonia's reaction, saying there was nothing wrong with her father aspiring for the top post. Sonia also revisits her 2004 decision to decline the prime minister's post.
title: Sonia was 'shocked' by Pranab's 'long-held desire' to be PM; his daughter asks why

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: During the electrifying NASCAR Cup Series championship race this past weekend, Sophie Cunningham took center stage, delivering pre-race instructions alongside Cole Swindell. With comedian Matt Rife donning her jersey during his show, the spotlight was on her, despite her recent first-round exit from the WNBA. Now an unrestricted free agent, speculation swirls about her future with the Indiana Fever and interest from other clubs as coaches assess her previous performances.
title: Sophie Cunningham reacts to Matt Rife wearing her jersey at NASCAR event

author: TOI Education
description: The Delhi government has declared November 16, 2026, a public holiday for Chhath Puja, also known as Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi. The holiday applies to all government offices, autonomous bodies and Public Sector Undertakings under the Delhi government. The General Administration Department issued the notification on November 9 with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor. The order will be published in the Delhi Gazette, Part IV (Extraordinary).
title: Delhi declares Nov 16 holiday for Chhath Puja; schools, offices shut

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Kyle Jamieson has expressed frustration over New Zealand's disrupted bowling attack due to injuries in the series against India. The absence of key bowlers like Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson has hindered the team's consistency. Jamieson mentioned that the lack of a settled bowling combination has affected their performance in challenges. He welcomed the favourable bowling conditions but acknowledged the transition to Test cricket ahead.

Celebrating alongside her husband Nick Jonas and daughter Malti, Priyanka also gears up for the highly anticipated release of her film 'Varanasi'.
title: Priyanka Chopra's Diwali gown took over 2,200 hours of embroidery

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A ranch in Oklahoma has been awarded for its sustainable management practices that support both cattle and wildlife. It implements rotational grazing across 25 paddocks to protect native grasslands and improve ecosystem health. The management system is designed to promote water conservation and soil retention properties. Wildlife species, including deer and various birds, benefit from the preserved habitat.
title: Oklahoma family's 10,000-acre ranch wins landowner of the year award

title: Man sold properties for Rs 48 lakh cash & paid capital gains tax, but faced penalty

author: SAHIL MALHOTRA
description: Persistent rain and repeated delays disrupted the third ODI at Seddon Park in Hamilton, with both India and New Zealand players waiting for the weather to clear. Despite a brief improvement and revised timings, another spell of rain forced abandonment. Fans endured hours of waiting, catching only fleeting glimpses of their favourite cricketers.
title: India vs New Zealand: How weather spoilt families' day out in Hamilton

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta launched the Namo Yamuna River Safari to promote eco-friendly tourism along the Yamuna River. The initiative features a 6-km round-trip cruise and recreational activities to engage visitors. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal and other officials highlighted its importance for cultural connection with the river. A musical fountain show and future water sports are planned to enhance the experience.
title: 'Namo Yamuna River Safari' launched in Delhi in bid to boost tourism; 6-km cruise planned

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly been urging President Donald Trump daily to resume military action against Iran. This comes as several Arab and Muslim leaders have advised Trump to pursue diplomatic avenues rather than escalate the conflict. Amid these discussions, Trump has indicated that further military intervention is not currently necessary. Iran has threatened to retaliate against any fresh US attacks, raising regional concerns.
title: Netanyahu's daily calls to Trump over Iran war spark pushback within White House: Report

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: In a dazzling display of talent, Aaryavir Sehwag smacked an impressive 160 runs against the UAE during the ACC U19 Asia Cup. His formidable innings featured 17 fours and seven sixes, paving the way for India's dominance. Partnering with VK Vineeth, they amassed a substantial 193 runs for the second wicket. However, he narrowly missed breaking the record for the highest Youth ODI score.
title: Aaryavir Sehwag joins Gill, Agarwal in elite list with stunning 160 against UAE

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan criticized Sonia Gandhi's memoir, arguing it attempts to whitewash the historical mistakes of the Congress party. He highlighted her emotional responses to key incidents while questioning her silence on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and other tragedies. The memoir details Sonia's childhood, her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi, and her experiences as part of the Gandhi family.
title: 'Should've called it Whitewashing, not Belonging': BJP mocks Sonia Gandhi's memoir

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Nvidia's board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, and the probe has exposed the AI chipmaker's biggest risk: it has no named successor. From CFO Colette Kress to Huang's children and son-in-law Nico Caprez, here's who could lead Nvidia next, and why analysts, investors and governance experts say replacing Huang won't be easy.
title: Nvidia CEO's Chinese 'spy' scandal raises a big question: Who comes after Jensen Huang?

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: The third ODI clash between India and New Zealand was marred by rain, resulting in its cancellation. Indian captain Shubman Gill opted to bowl after winning the toss. However, persistent rain caused major delays and eventually forced the game to be called off. India holds a 2-0 lead in the series, with New Zealand needing to secure victories in the upcoming matches scheduled for Mount Maunganui.
title: No play in Hamilton! Rain washes out third ODI, India remain 2-0 up

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Since August 2024, over 2,000 students and teachers have reportedly faced politically motivated persecution across Bangladesh. The persecution includes academic exclusion, physical attacks, and criminal proceedings targeting individuals linked to the Bangladesh Awami League. Numerous teachers have experienced exclusion from professional activities, physical assaults, and legal issues. JusticeMakers Bangladesh has called for independent investigations into these reported abuses.
title: Over 2,000 teachers, students face political persecution in Bangladesh: Report

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Prachi Shirodkar transitioned from her architecture studies to filmmaking. She produced a documentary exploring Goa's traditional goldsmith community, with her father's collaboration in writing. Though initially incomplete, the film received accolades at international festivals, including awards from Rotary International. Currently, she is based in Mumbai, working as an assistant director, further enhancing her filmmaking skills.
title: Goa filmmaker, 28, wins awards for low-budget film on traditional goldsmiths

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Eighteen-year-old Kobe stumbled upon a staggering €9 million in gold while performing drainage work in Belgium, finding the treasure ingeniously concealed behind a wall in a previously operational brewery. After alerting the property owner and law enforcement, an investigation commenced to unveil the treasure's history. With multiple stakeholders, including the current property owner and potential heirs to its original proprietor, the legal battle over ownership could drag on for years.
title: Workers find €9m in gold bars and coins hidden in Belgian cellar walls

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Cricket Scotland has decided to halt all cricket-related activities with Afghanistan, excluding ICC events, driven by serious concerns regarding the Taliban's treatment of women and broader human rights issues. This move underscores their dedication to promoting women's involvement in cricket. While ICC tournaments continue as planned, no bilateral series will be organised. The policy will be reassessed each year, or following significant progress in women's rights.
title: Why Scotland suspended cricket ties with Afghanistan outside ICC events

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: Novaya Gazeta, an independent newspaper critical of the Kremlin, has shut down its Moscow office after three decades. The closure came as a result of mounting government pressure and sustained restrictions on independent media. Journalists mourned the loss of their office while recalling the legacy of their investigative work. Some staff members have relocated abroad and continue reporting under a new publication called Novaya Gazeta Europe.
title: Six journalists killed: Russia's last major independent newspaper shuts down

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Jackson County in Missouri cancelled its request for bids on public land along the Blue River Parkway on November 9 after residents and conservation groups protested the proposed sale. The land has more than eight miles of volunteer-built trails used for hiking and mountain biking. Residents have called for stronger legal protection against future development.
title: Missouri county scraps sale of forest near golf course after residents protest

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Salman Butt faced an embarrassing moment while giving a pitch report for the first Test match. He repeatedly apologized as he struggled to maintain his composure on live television. The camera crew attempted to assist him by reminding him that they were live on air. This awkward moment quickly gained popularity on social media, leading to widespread sharing of the video.
title: 'We are live': Salman Butt's embarrassing on-air blunder goes viral - Watch

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: The Supreme Court has mandated that Delhi and three adjacent states intensify measures to combat vehicle emissions. Officials are tasked with reporting on the implementation of laws governing aging and non-compliant vehicles. With rising pollution levels in the National Capital Region, the court emphasized the need for inter-state collaboration on vehicle management and stricter adherence to emission standards. The matter will be reviewed again on November 23.
title: 'Warrants urgent attention': SC flags vehicle pollution in Delhi-NCR, seeks action plan

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
description: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, offers an intimate account of Indira Gandhi’s temper, recalling how staff were made to stand in corners, a senior Congress leader ordered to face a wall and others ignored for days. Sonia also describes Rajiv’s reassurance during her mother-in-law’s outbursts, Indira’s domestic routines, love for sarees and photographs, and how grandchildren gradually softened her temperament.
title: 'I'd quake in my seat': Sonia recalls Indira's temper, early days as bride in memoir

author: SAURABH SINHA
description: India’s capital, New Delhi, will attempt cloud seeding to induce rain and address severe pollution. The initiative involves Delhi International Airport Ltd, the Delhi government, and IIT Kanpur. A specialized aircraft from Kyathi Climate will undertake the operation on Tuesday and Wednesday. A fresh western disturbance is expected to bring rain to northwestern India later this week. Cloud seeding aims to enhance precipitation as the air quality deteriorates.
title: DIAL rains for relief: Choked Delhi to see another cloud seeding attempt

author: SANJAY SHARMA
description: A Stanford University review of 52 studies on AI in education highlights a key concern: students may complete assignments faster using generative AI without developing independent understanding. The November 2026 review found that AI shows greater promise when used to explain concepts, provide feedback and support practice rather than replace student thinking. While AI can improve learning experiences and save teachers' time, researchers say evidence of lasting improvements in academic performance remains insufficient.
title: Stanford study warns AI use may weaken students’ learning and critical thinking

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Asian stock markets rallied on Tuesday as US stocks experienced a significant rebound on the previous day. Notably, Japan's Nikkei 225 saw a 2.6% rise while South Korea's Kospi climbed 4%. Technology stocks led the gains with SoftBank Group shares jumping ahead of its earnings announcement. Concurrently, oil prices declined due to reduced military tensions regarding Iran's conflict situation.
title: Asian stocks rally as Wall Street rebounds, oil prices ease

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: INS Surat arrived in Muscat to join the 15th edition of Naseem Al Bahr and conduct joint patrols. The exercise fosters interoperability and strengthens cooperation between the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy of Oman. India maintains a presence in crucial maritime areas to ensure energy security and counter piracy threats. Recent operations showcased multi-national training initiatives and successful piracy rescues off the coast of Somalia.

Muse Ember emphasizes efficiency and cost-effectiveness for daily tasks across different applications.
title: Google CEO sends welcome note to Zuckerberg: Excited to serve our Cloud customer

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: In an inspiring effort to safeguard wildlife, villagers near Vellode Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu embrace a cracker-free Diwali tradition that spans over twenty years. Children are now enjoying the festival with sparklers, while the community comes together to wear new clothes and indulge in festive delicacies, celebrating both their culture and the revered ecology of the sanctuary, which draws numerous migratory birds each year.
title: Tamil Nadu villages skip Diwali crackers for 21 years to protect birds

description: Determined to protect an ancient wall from persistent thefts, an English mayor cleverly employed an Apple AirTag embedded in one of the coping stones. This initiative ultimately directed police to a thief in Wigan, who confessed to the charges. The recovered stones, estimated at £7,000, have revitalized community spirit, allowing local residents to rally together and restore this historic structure.
title: UK councillor hides AirTag in village wall stone, helps police catch thief

description: Mitchell Starc has once again addressed the controversy surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering incident, reaffirming his stance since 2021. Starc denied any involvement or knowledge of the tampering, insisting that the bowlers were kept in the dark about the matter.

An appeals court revised the homeowner's $170,000 award to $102,000, while upholding $50,000 in emotional distress damages under the nuisance claim.
title: Michigan business floods neighbour's basement; court cuts damages to $102,000

description: Manish Pralhad Ganveer and Sonali Ganveer were discovered dead at their home in Nagpur after Diwali celebrations. Their bodies were hanging from a ceiling fan and they had been married only in August. Relatives became concerned when they could not reach the couple and sent someone to check on them. Neighbors reported hearing an argument before the house fell silent on Friday afternoon.
title: 2nd marriage, locked house, unanswered calls: Mystery shrouds deaths of Nagpur couple

author: PRACHI KUMAWAT
description: Dhami village in Himachal Pradesh observes a unique stone-pelting ritual called 'Patthar Ka Khel' after Diwali. This tradition involves two groups of villagers throwing stones at each other until someone gets injured. Following the ritual, blood from the injured participant is offered to Goddess Bhadrakali. The ceremony is thought to have originated as a substitute for human sacrifice to appease the deity.
title: Why villagers pelt each other with stones in Himachal's 400-year-old tradition

author: SIDDHI DHARMADHIKARI
description: Punjab experienced a total of 4,657 stubble burning incidents reported until November 9, 2026. Police have filed 1,442 FIRs, and environmental fines totaling Rs 7.285 crore were imposed and partially recovered. The district of Tarn Taran had the highest number of incidents with 659 reported cases. Monitoring teams are actively inspecting and addressing stubble burning violations in several districts.
title: Punjab records 4,657 stubble-burning cases; 1,442 FIRs, Rs 7.28 crore in fines

The FBI is scrutinizing the implications on national security concerning Nvidia's technology and partnerships.
